figures.alt: Historic wood double-hung window with a removed lower sash and localized sill repair condition
figures.caption: Start by distinguishing repairable sash and sill deterioration from a full replacement need. Preservation work is scope-sensitive: the correct answer depends on water path, wood condition, operation, and historic character.
figures.before: Why Windows Are a Defining Feature in Historic Preservation Review

figures.alt: Window opening with sill flashing membrane formed into a drainage pan
figures.caption: If replacement or major repair is required, give the opening a reliable drainage strategy. New or restored windows still depend on the sill and flashing details around them.
figures.before: What Self-Perform Framing Changes on Window Replacement Projects

figures.alt: Finished exterior window trim with a sloped sill and narrow caulk joint
figures.caption: Finish trim and sealant should direct water outward without trapping it. The visible exterior joint is only the last layer of the window's water-management assembly.
figures.before: Exterior Trim and Casing: The Finishing Detail That Matters
